# Samuccayakkhandhaka (Kd 13)

**ID:** Kd 13  
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Samuccayakkhandhaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

A notable textual feature is the concluding colophon to the chapter, which explicitly identifies the lineage of transmission: *ācariyānaṁ vibhajjavādānaṁ tambapaṇṇidīpapasādakānaṁ mahāvihāravāsinam vācanā saddhammatthitiyā* ("This is the recitation of the Vibhajyavādin teachers, who brought faith to the island of Tambapaṇṇi, the dwellers of the Mahāvihāra, for the preservation of the True Dhamma") [Skilling; Kang-yuan Sung 1999]. Scholars highlight this colophon as vital evidence for the redactional activity and final formalisation of the Theravāda Vinaya within the Mahāvihāra tradition of Sri Lanka [Skilling; Kang-yuan Sung 1999].

 An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd12 Pudgalavastu; xct-mu-kd12 Samuccaya; lzh-mu-kd12 Samuccaya; Lzh Sarv Kd12a a. Samuccaya Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 12 Samuccaya Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 10a a. Samuccaya Khandhaka
- Resembling parallels: Lzh Mg Bu Pn2 Vagga 2. Ukkhepanīya; san-mu-kd13 Pudgalavastu; xct-mu-kd13 Parivāsa; lzh-mu-kd13 Parivāsa; Lzh Sarv Kd12b b. Parivāsa Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 13 Parivāsa Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 16 Parivāsa Khandhaka; Kd 12 Pārivāsikakkhandhaka

**Sources**

- [Frauwallner 1956] Erich Frauwallner, The Earliest Vinaya and the Beginnings of Buddhist Literature (1956) — Confirmed sequence and numbering of the Cullavagga khandhakas.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pāli Literature (1983) — Provided English translation title 'Accumulation (of offences)' and Khandhaka context.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, A Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Corroborated correspondence to the Pudgalavastu.
- [Skilling] Peter Skilling, 'Theravāda in History' — Provided citation and translation of the Mahāvihāra/Vibhajyavādin colophon at the end of the text.
- [Kang-yuan Sung 1999] Kang-yuan Sung, 'Tradition and Development in the Mo-ho-seng-ch’i-lu (Mahāsāṃghika)' (1999) — Discussed the Sri Lankan editorial incorporation of the uddāna/colophon mentioning the Mahāvihāra.
- [Vinayamukha 1983] Entrance to the Vinaya: Vinayamukha, Vol. 3 (1983) — Detailed the vuṭṭhānavidhi procedures, parivāsa, mānatta, and legal formulas (kammavācā) such as that for Ven. Udāyi.
